title: Strict tower preservation from amplification and witnesses
statement: Let square be a chosen Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] of schemes X, Y, Xprime, Yprime, all Noetherian, with its two vertical morphisms proper. Let d be an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. If AMP(square; c) of [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification] holds for some natural number c, and WIT(square) of [def-weil-pbc-witness-compatibility] holds, then TOW(square) of [def-weil-pbc-tower-preservation] holds: all four actual strict completed-coefficient tower functors preserve uniformly bounded constructible adic towers with quotient-linear levels, transition and normalization data, and common local models compatible with every interval containment supplied by AMP.

proof.text: The input common bounded local complexes tensor the uniform finite projective quotient resolutions in one interval [d0-r,d1]. The constant-to-completed flat comparison transports these bounds to the restricted completed coefficients. Input cohomology is intrinsically constructible, so normalized local effectivity supplies bounded constructible etale origin. AMP gives the finite direct-image intervals [d0-r,d1+c] and the finite pullback intervals [d0-r,d1].

Take the finite images as quotient-linear output levels. Direct-image evaluation and restriction comparison identify them with the evaluations of the strict tower functor. WIT and the coefficient projection formula give normalized reductions inducing the actual transitions and cocycle. On pullbacks, objectwise K-flat tensor and the constant/completed finite quotient identities give Bprime tensor over B with S_n equals S_n. Tensor reassociation therefore identifies finite pullbacks with evaluations of completed pullback on the supplied quotient-linear levels. Naturality gives all transition equations, and WIT gives normalization and the cocycle.

Apply normalized constructible local effectivity to the output adic towers to get uniform constructibility and common local models. For every cprime satisfying AMP and every input-level window [a,b], the same argument gives finite output windows [a,b+cprime] for direct image and [a,b] for pullback. The local-effectivity construction truncates a finite-type local model in that same interval, retaining its derived reductions and normalization maps. Thus the already specified output towers have HasTowerAmplitudeCompatibleModels as well. Assemble the four preservation predicates.

theorem towerPreservation_of_amplification_witnesses
    {X' X Y' Y : Scheme.{u}}
    {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y}
    (sq : ChosenCartesianSquare g' f' f g)
    {A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] (d : Scheme.AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y] [IsNoetherian X'] [IsNoetherian Y']
    [IsProper f] [IsProper f'] (c : ℕ)
    (hAmp : Scheme.HasFiniteLevelAmplification sq d c)
    (hWit : WitnessCompatibility sq d) : Scheme.HasTowerPreservation sq d
